validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE CONFIRMED, INDEPENDENT OF GEM, WITH THE 'COMMON PLACE NAME' RISK EXPLICITLY RULED OUT. This is a real, FERC-jurisdictional, gas transmission pipeline sponsored by Lower Valley Energy (a rural electric/gas cooperative serving Star Valley, WY and Bear Lake County, ID), running from Montpelier, ID to Afton, WY (Star Valley), authorized under FERC Docket CP20-461 (and a related U.S. Forest Service special-use permit through Caribou-Targhee National Forest). Independent origins corroborating the SAME project, in the SAME location, with the SAME sponsor (not merely a same-named 'Crow Creek' elsewhere): (1) EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, Aug2026 release, sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' row 33 -- 'Crow Creek Pipeline', Pipeline Operator Name 'Lower Valley Energy Coop', ID/WY, 49 mi; (2) Wayback capture of the FAST-41 Federal Permitting Dashboard project page (live URL 403s scripted clients; capture at web.archive.org/web/20260313230614/https://www.permits.performance.gov/permitting-project/other-projects/crow-creek-pipeline-project) naming the project, the Forest Service as lead federal agency, and the Montpelier-Afton corridor; (3) DOJ Office of Public Affairs press release, 2025-07-29 ('Justice Department Secures Win for American Energy: Crow Creek Natural Gas Pipeline'), reporting a federal court's denial of a preliminary injunction sought by opponents (Western Watersheds Project/Center for Biological Diversity types) against Forest Service authorization, naming the pipeline, the two termini, and Lower Valley Energy; (4) Pipeline & Gas Journal, 2025-07-29, reporting the same injunction denial and construction start; (5) Jackson Hole News & Guide, reporting on the project and the litigation, naming Lower Valley Energy and the Star Valley service territory; (6) two federal court dockets (District of Idaho and 9th Circuit, via CourtListener/PACER public docket pages) captioned around the Forest Service's Crow Creek authorization, with September 2025 entries including photographic exhibits of active pipe installation and trench backfilling -- used as context/existence corroboration only, NOT staged as a proposed_refs source on any fills[] record, because the docket page itself (case caption text) does not literally name 'Crow Creek Pipeline' on the page tested by url_verifier (fails name_found; the docket concerns 'Afton'-captioned litigation) -- a deliberate exclusion per the rule that a page must name the project, not just be about it. Six-plus independent origins, several explicitly naming this exact sponsor/location/docket, decisively rule out both a thin same-name coincidence and a GEM-only/hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION: gas transmission (NGA-adjacent Forest Service ROW/FERC-adjacent interstate delivery pipeline serving a cooperative's distribution system, not a gathering/process line) -- correct as recorded; Fuel=Gas correct. DUPLICATE: no other row in the 42-row A7 roster describes this Montpelier ID-Afton WY corridor or this sponsor; not a relabel of any other PID. CAVEAT (why 'caveat' not a clean confirm): (a) EIA's Aug2026 release states Diameter=12in against the sheet's/permits.gov's/P&GJ's 8in -- flagged below as a spec concern favoring the sheet's 8in figure; (b) the sheet's ProposalYear=2020 is plausible but soft -- EIA's own project notes reference an original U.S. Forest Service Record of Decision issued November 2019 (later withdrawn in 2022 after litigation, then re-authorized via a Final Supplemental EIS), which is earlier than the 2020 Seattle Times/AP article currently cited for ProposalYear; no independently dated pre-2020 filing/announcement was found to pin an exact earlier proposal date, so the existing 2020 citation is kept (REVERIFIED) rather than overwritten with an unsourced 2019 guess, but the tension is noted here as a soft attribution/spec caveat, contested left blank (evidence says the current year may be slightly late, no confident replacement date). Neither caveat rises to existence/duplicate/classification doubt.

validity.researcher_notes: EIA's Aug2026 Natural Gas Pipeline Projects release (sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects', row 33) states Diameter=12in for this project, disagreeing with the sheet's recorded 8in. However, two independent sources describe an 8-inch, not 12-inch, line: the FAST-41 permits.performance.gov project page (Wayback capture) and Pipeline & Gas Journal's 2025-07-29 article both describe an eight-inch, low-pressure distribution-feeder-scale pipeline (consistent with Lower Valley Energy's stated purpose of replacing overland LNG trucking into the Star Valley service area with a small local supply line, not a large-diameter interstate trunk). EIA's own project notes describe it as a 'High-pressure pipeline,' which is internally inconsistent with an 8-inch NPS at typical local-distribution pressures and reads as though it may reflect a data-entry error or conflation with a different, larger project in the same docket family. Weighing 2 independent sources (permits.gov + P&GJ) describing 8in, one of them contemporaneous with actual construction, against EIA's single 12in figure: the sheet's 8in value is better corroborated. Recommending no change to the recorded Diameter, with EIA's conflicting figure flagged here rather than silently accepted; contested left as "" (evidence says EIA's own value is more likely wrong, not that the sheet's needs a specific new number).

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The sheet's Status=proposed (LastUpdated 2025-09-16) is stale. DOJ (2025-07-29) and Pipeline & Gas Journal (2025-07-29) both report a federal court's denial of a preliminary injunction against the Forest Service's authorization, clearing the way for construction to begin in July 2025. Further, federal court docket entries in the related District of Idaho/9th Circuit litigation (via CourtListener/PACER public docket pages, examined for existence corroboration though not cited here as a proposed_refs source since the docket page text itself does not name 'Crow Creek Pipeline' verbatim -- fails the name_found bar) include exhibits dated around September 2025 showing photographs of active pipe installation and trench backfilling along the route, i.e. physical construction in progress, not merely authorized-to-begin. EIA's Aug2026 release still reads project status 'Approved' (as of its 2026-05 status-change entry) rather than 'Under Construction' or 'Completed', which lags the on-the-ground evidence by roughly a year -- EIA's periodic-release cadence is the likely explanation, not a reason to doubt the two contemporaneous, independent, dated news sources. Recommending Status=construction with ConstructionYear=2025, consistent with the existing (re-verified) Construction [ref] fill above. Evidence_date reflects the September 2025 photographic construction evidence as the most recent independently-dated confirmation found (the July sources establish the legal clearance and expected start; the September docket exhibits are the most recent dated evidence of physical progress, though excluded from proposed_refs on the name-found technicality -- noted here in full per the exhaustive-reading rule). No independent source yet states the project has been completed/placed in service, so 'operating' is not supported -- 'construction' is the evidence-supported verdict.
